A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TCEC research. All 18 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: V2 reports original image and video generation evaluations, compensation and regularization ablations, error visualizations, and inference latency measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds Jacobian measurements, inference-step and calibration-size studies, and CIFAR-10 comparisons.

M1.justification: The compensation procedure, channel-wise calibration objective, regularization rule and solver adaptations remain unchanged. Equation 4 now explicitly uses the perturbed input, consistent with downstream compensation formulas already present in v2.

E1.justification: Appendix J adds CIFAR-10 image-generation evaluation at 32×32 resolution; v2 mentions CIFAR-10 only when discussing prior work. Existing image/video datasets remain covered, and the video models moved into Table 3 already appeared in v2's appendix.

E2.justification: The new CIFAR-10 comparison evaluates QNCD and Q-Diffusion. QNCD was previously citation-only, while Q-Diffusion was already evaluated on OpenSora. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: V3 substantially expands evaluation settings: CIFAR-10 uses 50,000 generated samples, 100/250-step DDIM, W4A8/W4A6 and IS/FID/sFID. Additional studies introduce two/three-step SDXL-Turbo inference and calibration sizes of 256, 512 and 2048. Previously reported benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A measures the discarded Jacobian contribution at three SDXL timesteps; Appendix G investigates minimal effective inference steps; Appendix I tests calibration-set size. These materially expand validation beyond the retained error-accumulation, regularization and visualization analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. V3 calls small gains experimental noise but provides no corresponding uncertainty estimate or estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V3 adds Jacobian magnitudes, two/three-step results, calibration-size outcomes and CIFAR-10 comparisons in Tables 4 and 7–9. For example, the new W4A6/DDIM-100 comparison reports FID 12.26 for QNCD and 10.76 for TCEC. Retained benchmark, ablation and latency values match v2.

T1.justification: Appendix A introduces quantitative bounds, including a Lipschitz constant below 0.3 and a coefficient magnitude at most 0.05, to justify neglecting the Jacobian. Equation 4 also corrects the error-evaluation input. The existing error recursion, m=1 argument and DPM++ derivation remain intact.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same cumulative-error framework, novelty, solver compatibility and PTQ orthogonality claims, including the 1.2 PSNR improvement and less-than-0.5% overhead. Additional experiments support rather than redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive explanations of Jacobian negligibility, limited benefits below three inference steps, calibration saturation around 1024 samples and stronger compensation benefits at lower activation precision. It also argues calibration-domain insensitivity through VAE/DiT processing, reinterpreting the retained WebVid/VBench evidence.

D1.justification: Appendix J specifies BRECQ and AdaRound for the new four-bit-weight experiments and reports TAC/QNCD code availability. The hardware discussion clarifies which retained timing comparisons reuse ViDiT-Q versus SVDQuant engines, while dropping the explicit Nunchaku name. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: The bibliography retains the same works. Section 2.2 replaces generic criticism of earlier correction approaches with specific descriptions of TAC and QNCD, sharpening their distinction from cumulative-error compensation. Appendix J further explains the choice of QNCD for comparison.

P1.justification: Most existing scientific prose and section order are retained. Local revisions expand related-work, hardware and approximation explanations, add appendix cross-references, remove the LLM-usage statement and introduce an Impact Statement. The added scientific sections do not amount to wholesale narrative rewriting.

P2.justification: V3 reformats the main text and references into two columns and resizes or relocates displays throughout. It adds four tables and merges v2's main-text and appendix latency tables into Table 3 with revised columns. Figures 1–4 retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: The new QNCD comparison and sensitivity studies supply useful evidence missing in v2. However, Appendix A reports sqrt(alpha[t−1]/alpha[t]) below one, contradicting Section 3.1's decreasing-alpha definition. Tables 7–8 label sums of FID/PSNR gains as 'Avg', while Appendix G asserts an experimental-noise threshold without uncertainty estimates. These empirical benefits and new problems with the supporting reasoning leave the net quality direction unclear.
